audit.summary: Incorrect Student-t degrees of freedom in the FIV approximation and a false predictive ground-truth collapse affect theoretical model properties. Released SLP code uses predictive covariance in the mean, with historical experimental effect unresolved. Reported average percentage improvements match table arithmetic.
limitations: Limitations: No author code, optimizer or backtest executed; no historical empirical attribution established.
Limitations: Actual PDF is 28 pages; source manifest's 52 is an extraction-control-character artifact preserved separately.
Limitations: Full joint-model interpretation of the FIV mixture remains Needs Evidence.
Limitations: Separate OpenReview attachments unavailable; later revisions/errata not independently inspected.
Limitations: All main and applicable appendix text read, but not all background results and implementation files independently verified.

P1 — FIV Normal–inverse-Wishart marginal has wrong degrees of freedom — Counterevidence: m=1 degrees coincide; no claim that the SLP experiments use FIV. The paper explicitly calls the FIV hierarchy an approximation, but the integral under its stated hierarchy is still exact and incorrect.

P2 — Perfect views do not eliminate intrinsic predictive noise — Counterevidence: Latent theta does collapse with full-rank exact views; P=I in practical appendix avoids rank issue but not intrinsic return noise.

P3 — Released mean uses predictive covariance multiplier — Counterevidence: Pinned repository is a later refactor and its older file is not proof of which code generated the paper. No original experiment rerun.
P4 — Predictive corollary precision/inverse omissions — Counterevidence: Adjacent theorems and proofs give correct expressions; gamma=1 avoids first discrepancy.
Limitations: Focused acceptance of reported issues only; initial full-paper coverage is not claimed as independently repeated.
The original report's complete scope, counterevidence and unresolved questions are retained below.
This import checks publication format and identity; it does not repeat scientific review.
Independent human scientific review is pending; author adoption has not been requested.

proposition.claim:
Normal mean with IW(Psi',nu') covariance has t_nu' marginal and scale Psi'/(nu'-m+1).

Omega tends to zero and accurate classical views imply predictive returns converge to delta_rstar.

Released BL mean computation corresponds to the proposed posterior mean.

The displayed corollaries follow their preceding Gaussian posteriors.

t_(nu'-m+1)(mu',Psi'/(nu'-m+1)); E[S]=Psi'/(nu'-m-1) when nu'>m+1.
